summary: For a random 3-dimensional grid of numbers, how many simple product pieces are needed to build it, as a dimension count predicts?
note: Friedland conjecture; numerics support it, but a general proof needs major algebraic geometry.

summary: Start with any nonempty list of integers and keep appending its curling number; the list eventually reaches curling number 1.
note: Simple rule with experimental support; no general argument known, needs a genuinely new idea.

summary: Points in 3D space define polynomials; the conjecture says these polynomials are always linearly independent when the points are distinct.
note: Linear-algebra flavour tied to geometry; a short argument might exist but none is known here.

summary: For every length k, are there infinitely many primes that start a chain of exactly k primes, each equal to twice the previous plus one?
note: Prime-pattern question in the Dickson family; far beyond current sieve and prime-distribution methods.

summary: Adding consecutive terms, dividing composites by their least prime, must eventually repeat a cycle for every pair of positive starting integers.
note: Prime-dependent dynamics with no invariant or potential function known; computation alone cannot prove it.

summary: For numbers called crystals, only one pair of factors makes the number a crystal.
note: Divisibility-style claim that may be provable directly; the defining formula is not given in the file.

summary: The longest possible s-increasing sequence of r-tuples has length at most n to the power three halves.
note: Extremal combinatorics with an explicit power bound; the file gives no proof route.

summary: Barker sequences are lists of plus and minus ones with small off-peak correlations; none is longer than 13 terms, the conjecture says.
note: Exhaustive searches cover many lengths, but no general argument rules out all longer sequences.

summary: For every exponent n above 8, writing two to the power n in base three always produces a digit two.
note: Equivalent to a Busy Beaver halting question; likely needs a deep number-theory argument or a computation-based proof.

summary: Can a bounded shape full of holes, with positive area, in two or more dimensions be spectral, meaning it has a special family of wave patterns?
note: Fourier-analysis problem; the one-dimensional case is settled negatively, higher dimensions lack a route.

summary: The only atom-free probability measure on the circle invariant under both multiplying angles by p and multiplying by q is the uniform one.
note: Furstenberg's famous conjecture; deep ergodic theory with only partial results over decades.

summary: A specific sum built from the classical theta function stays positive for every odd prime k.
note: Numerical checks are easy; a proof likely needs modular-form identities, a specialist method.

summary: Bounded orbits of the diagonal group acting on lattice space SL_n(R)/SL_n(Z) are always closed, for matrix size at least 3.
note: Known for function fields; the real case needs homogeneous-dynamics machinery and is a major open problem.

summary: In every regular graph, the independent domination number is at most the saturation number.
note: Machine-generated finite graph inequality; could yield to a counting argument or a small counterexample search.

summary: Every graph whose vertices all have at least k neighbours contains a cycle whose length is a multiple of k.
note: Known for k=3 and 4; the k=5 case is the one left open in this file.

summary: In a highly connected graph with large minimum degree, any path avoiding a longest cycle has at most k minus one vertices.
note: Extremal graph theory with an explicit degree threshold; partial results exist, the general case is open.

summary: The tangent of the sum arctan 1 plus arctan 2 up to arctan n is never an integer when n is at least 5.
note: Elementary statement; known special cases, but a general proof likely needs algebraic number theory.

summary: Every bridgeless simple graph can be covered by cycles whose total length is at most seven fifths of its edge count.
note: Famous cycle-cover bound; the constant 7/5 is far beyond known general results.

summary: For N below roughly two to the n, no set of n residues modulo N gives all distinct multiset sums.
note: Finite residue question checkable for small n; a general proof needs a structural lemma.

summary: Must every separable normed space whose isometries move any unit vector to any other be a Hilbert space?
note: Famous functional-analysis problem with decades of partial results and no known full route.

summary: Is the cohomology ring of every finite-dimensional Hopf algebra finitely generated?
note: Etingof-Ostrik conjecture; deep homological algebra, a major open problem.

summary: Must every ring endomorphism of the first Weyl algebra, the polynomial differential operators, be an automorphism?
note: Tied to the Jacobian conjecture family; decades old and no clear route.

summary: Must Poisson-bracket-preserving polynomial maps in one variable be invertible, the Poisson analogue of the Dixmier question?
note: Implied by the hard Jacobian problem and implies Dixmier; expected to be very hard.

summary: For torsion-free groups, every finitely generated projective module over the integer group ring is stably free.
note: Conditional on the deep Farrell-Jones conjecture, which the file does not supply; needs algebraic K-theory.

summary: Is there a transcendental number a and positive x with x times a to the n close to an integer as n grows?
note: Diophantine approximation of power sequences; transcendence tools are insufficient, open for decades.

summary: Find a very fast-growing integer sequence whose multiples by every irrational number are spread densely modulo one.
note: Weaker growth notions have constructions; the strong ratio reading is open and needs new ideas.

summary: For a Pisot number above two and any point in its Cantor-type set, powers of that point are not evenly spread modulo one.
note: Plausible via digit expansions of Pisot numbers, but a specialist problem with no proof in the file.

summary: Are there arbitrarily large non-Pisot real numbers whose powers all have fractional parts lying in one short interval?
note: Construction question; a clever explicit family could settle it, but no route is known.

summary: For every real number and prime p, a product of distance to the nearest integer, size and p-adic size can get arbitrarily small.
note: Analogue of the famous Littlewood conjecture; the p-adic version over the rationals remains open.

summary: No real number has all fractional parts of its powers of three-halves below one half, for every positive power.
note: Mahler's Z-number question; special cases known, the general statement is open.

summary: Are the fractional parts of three-halves raised to the n evenly spread between zero and one?
note: Open variant follows from compactness of the circle, so as stated it looks trivial; check the formalisation.

summary: In a finite abelian group with a dense set A, are there many 10-tuples where specified sums of pairs all land in A?
note: Counting problem with a specific exponent; Cauchy-Schwarz-type methods might give it, unclear.

summary: Write down an explicit two-colouring of the first 2r squared minus one integers with no monochromatic 3-term or r-term progression, for some r.
note: The explicit construction is the hard part; exact values for larger r rely on heavy computation.

summary: Is there a Lipschitz function from the naturals to the integers whose graph contains no three points forming an arithmetic progression?
note: Construction question; an explicit or probabilistic construction might settle it, nothing known.

summary: What is the largest subset of 1 to N with no solution to x plus 3y equal to 2z plus 2w in distinct integers?
note: Extremal counting with unknown growth order; usually needs Fourier and density-increment tools.

summary: In a finite group, if a set of pairs has positive density, do many triples x, y, g give three pairs all inside that set?
note: Abelian corners theory covers the commutative case; the general group version is a research question.

summary: Given n integers, can we pick about (log n) to the 100 of them whose pairwise sums of distinct picks all avoid the original set?
note: Polylog-size subset question; a density or greedy argument might work, but no known route.

summary: For integer equations that fail Rado's condition, is the number of colours needed to avoid monochromatic solutions bounded by the number of variables?
note: Rado boundedness conjecture from 1933, open for four or more variables; Ramsey-theoretic and hard.

summary: For any r-colouring of 1 to N with N large, can we find x and y at least 3 where x plus y and x times y share a colour?
note: Asks for better bounds on a known threshold, not a yes-no; needs quantitative sum-product ideas.

summary: Given n integers, how many affine copies of the pattern 0, 1, 3 can the set contain? Conjectured to be about n squared over three.
note: Asymptotic extremal question with a conjectured constant; Cauchy-Schwarz style bounds may help.

summary: For which numbers k does splitting 1 to N into k classes always make the within-class sums cover at least a tenth of N?
note: Asymptotic threshold question with a gap between known bounds; sharpening needs new combinatorial input.

summary: Over a finite prime field, can the whole space always be covered by a bounded number of cube-shaped sets?
note: The formal statement looks suspicious; the question needs clarifying before anyone attacks it.

summary: What is the smallest set of residues mod p, with at least two elements, where no sum has exactly one representation?
note: Unique-sum problem with known bounds; exact growth unclear and no obvious method.

summary: If two independent whole-number random variables sum to a uniform distribution, must each one be uniform on its own range too?
note: Cyclotomic polynomial factorisation looks like a viable route; no counterexample is known.

summary: Can we beat the square-root lower bound for the largest Sidon subset of 1 to N, at least for infinitely many N?
note: Erdos-type Sidon problem; upper bounds have improved recently, but constructions beating the lower bound are harder.

summary: For about root-p residues mod a prime p, does some multiple of that set miss a run of 100 root-p consecutive residues?
note: Dilate-gap question; a Fourier-type method may work, but nothing in the file suggests one.

summary: Are there infinitely many moduli q with a residue set of size about sqrt(2q) whose pairwise sums cover every residue mod q?
note: Additive-basis construction in cyclic groups; explicit families might suffice, none is known.

summary: For each exponent p above one, how small can the L^p norm of the self-convolution of a nonnegative unit-integral function on [0,1] be?
note: Constant improvement via numerics or clever test functions; hard to formalise in Lean analysis.

summary: Do large abelian groups exist with n pairs of subsets whose sumsets are pairwise disjoint and of full product size?
note: Tied to fast matrix multiplication (Cohn-Kleinberg-Szegedy-Umans); a deep group-theoretic question.

summary: What is the smallest set of whole numbers containing, for each difference up to N, a k-term progression with that difference?
note: Small cases are computable; the asymptotic lower bound is conjectural and needs new combinatorics.

summary: Can we lower the best known exponential upper bound on the largest admissible set size in Green's graph-capacity-type problem?
note: Improving an exponential bound on a Shannon-capacity-type quantity; incremental and hard to predict.

summary: For a random set of about root-p residues mod prime p, is it almost surely covered by 100 root-p translates of the set?
note: Naive random covering needs about root-p log p translates, so the constant 100 looks very delicate.

summary: What is the largest product-free set in the alternating group A_n, a set where no product of two members lies in the set?
note: Group-theoretic extremal problem with known bounds only; exact answer needs representation theory.

summary: Does a covering-type quantity f(r) indexed by r grow without bound as r increases?
note: Definition is not in the file; f equal to 1 for all r is not ruled out, so boundedness is possible.

summary: How many rotated copies of a pyjama-shaped set about the origin are needed to cover the plane, as its width shrinks?
note: Known triple-exponential bound; removing one exponential needs a sharper geometric argument.

summary: After removing half the residue classes modulo each of 1000 primes below N to the 0.9, is at most a tenth of N left?
note: Sieve heuristics point to yes; error terms from the large primes make a rigorous proof delicate.

summary: Can we pick one residue class for each prime up to N so that every integer up to N lies in at least ten chosen classes?
note: Covering-system question; reciprocal prime sums grow so it is plausible, but the construction is delicate.

summary: What is the largest y such that the integers 1 to y can be covered by residue classes, one per prime up to x?
note: Improving a known lower bound by construction; plausible with sharper covering systems, hard in general.

summary: If a set of integers occupies about half the residues modulo every prime, must most of it lie on the values of a quadratic polynomial?
note: Large-sieve inverse theory with deep analytic tools; the finite-exception version is still hard.

summary: What is the best exponent alpha such that every nontrivial finite group of order n has a product-free set of size about n to the alpha?
note: Kedlaya gives 11/14; sharpness is conjectured via Ree groups, but no method is in sight.

summary: For a dense subset A of F_2^n, does its 10-fold sumset contain a large affine subspace whose codimension depends only on log density?
note: Additive combinatorics over F_2; Bogolyubov-type tools may reach it, but the log dependence is delicate.

summary: For a dense subset A of F_2^n, how large a subspace coset is guaranteed inside 2A? Near density one half, is codimension bounded?
note: Exact guaranteed-size function is hard to pin down; the near-one-half variant is the attackable part.

summary: If a set in F_2^n has a small additive complement of size K, must its doubled sumset contain a coset of bounded codimension in K?
note: Finite-field structure with a clean bounded-codimension target; specialist-level, no known route.

summary: If F_2^n is partitioned into K sets, must some doubled set 2A_i contain a coset of codimension bounded in K?
note: Partition version of the previous problem; finite objects, but a pigeonhole-style argument is not obvious.

summary: If two subsets of 1 to N each have at least N^0.49 elements, must some sum from them be composite?
note: Parity forces each set to have one parity; the remaining odd-even case needs a prime-sum argument.

summary: Is there a fixed c > 0 so that any set of at least two squares has pairwise-sum set at least size |A| to the power 1+c?
note: Sumset growth for squares; known sum-product style techniques may help but no direct route.

summary: If sums of pairs from A include the first n squares, must A have size close to n? Known bounds are n^(2/3) below and n over polylog above.
note: Erdos-Newman problem; improving the known two-thirds exponent to 1 needs a new idea.

summary: For a large prime p, is every nonzero residue mod p a product of two primes less than p?
note: Erdos-Odlyzko-Sarkozy question; covering all residues needs deep prime distribution, not a clever trick.

summary: Are there infinitely many primes p where p minus 2 has an odd number of prime factors counted with multiplicity?
note: Statement is elementary but parity of shifted primes is twin-prime-hard; sieve results fall short.

summary: Is there always a sum of two squares between X minus a small power of X and X, for large X?
note: Short-interval sums-of-two-squares problem; current gap bounds are analytic and weaker than needed.

summary: Does Ulam's sequence, defined by unique sums of earlier terms, have positive density, and why is its Fourier behaviour curious?
note: Erdos problem 342; no known method for density, and Fourier structure is unexplained.

summary: What is the largest set of grid points with no three on a line? Can an N by N grid hold 2N such points for large N?
note: Classic no-three-in-line; large-k case is known, small k and the exact size remain open.

summary: Given n points in the unit disc, must some triangle formed by them have area at most n to the power -2 plus small error?
note: Heilbronn-type triangle problem; best known bounds are far from n to the power -2.

summary: For a set of n integers, how few angles theta in the circle make the cosine sum vanish? The answer is a specific minimal zero-count function.
note: Needs exact Littlewood-type analytic estimates; recent progress is partial, not a clean argument.

summary: If an open set in the unit square has area alpha, must four of its points form an axis-parallel rectangle of area at least a constant times alpha squared?
note: Geometric and plausible, but needs measure-theory setup and known Carbery-type machinery.

summary: Does the five-term arithmetic progression-free count r_5(N) fall below N over a log power? Also a finite-field 4-term version.
note: Finite-field F_5 variant may suit polynomial-method counting; unverified. Integer version needs density increment.

summary: Must every locally compact topological group acting faithfully on a connected manifold be a Lie group? Hilbert's fifth problem in general form.
note: Famous Hilbert-Smith conjecture; only special dimensions known, needs major new ideas.

summary: If finite groups G and H have equal order and equal sum of Euler totients of element orders, and G is simple, must H be simple?
note: Plausibly reducible to classification-level facts about simple groups; no clear route yet.

summary: Do simple groups exist that are pro-orderable, meaning built as inverse limits of orderable groups?
note: Existence question; a clever construction could settle it, but definitional details matter.

summary: If a group is the product of two normal subgroups that are both Engel-type nilgroups, is the whole group a nilgroup?
note: Fitting-type analogue for Engel groups; plausible structural argument, but not known.

summary: Describe all non-discrete Hausdorff topological groups whose proper closed subgroups are all discrete.
note: Open-ended classification; only the locally compact case is understood.

summary: For a p-group where abelian normal subgroups have order at most p to the k, do all abelian subgroups have order at most p to the 2k?
note: Finite p-group bound; a counting or Pyber-style argument might work, but unresolved.

summary: Is there a non-cyclic finitely presented group containing an element whose powers reach every element up to conjugacy?
note: Existence question; a clever construction could settle it, but none is known.

summary: If the coefficients of a power series solving an algebraic differential equation are integral after inverting some N, must the series be algebraic?
note: Needs arithmetic-geometry machinery on differential equations; no elementary route.

summary: If 2 to the x and 3 to the x are both integers, must x be an integer?
note: Rational case is easy; irrational case needs transcendence theory on logarithms.

summary: Is there a polynomial in two rational variables that gives a bijection from pairs of rationals to rationals?
note: Polynomial bijection question over Q; known rigidity results for integers may extend.

summary: For a bijection of R^n, if the induced power-set map is connected, is the inverse map's power-set map also connected?
note: Topology question with a plausibly short argument; obscure, single-source origin.

summary: If a product of two monic polynomials with nonnegative coefficients has only 0 and 1 coefficients, must each factor also have only 0 and 1 coefficients?
note: Polynomial factorization question; a short argument or counterexample may settle it.

summary: Can a unit square be covered by rectangles of sides 1/(n+1) by 1/(n+2) for all n?
note: Total area is exactly one, forcing rigid tiling-like structure; the answer is unclear.

summary: Are primes among sums of the first 2m primes distributed like m over log m, with a density factor of two?
note: Needs analytic prime distribution in a sparse sequence; no clever shortcut apparent.

summary: Is the integer complexity of 2 to the n equal to 2n, the fewest ones needed to write it with addition, multiplication and parentheses?
note: Known lower bounds for integer complexity fall short of 2n; needs a sharper argument.

summary: Weak Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture: links the rank of an elliptic curve to the behaviour of its L-function at one.
note: Clay Millennium problem; decades of expert work, needs a major breakthrough.

summary: Do smooth solutions to the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes fluid equations exist for all time from smooth initial data?
note: Clay Millennium problem; requires deep PDE analysis, no clever argument known.

summary: Is every smooth four-dimensional manifold homeomorphic to the sphere the same as the standard smooth sphere? Smooth version of Poincare conjecture in dimension four.
note: Famous smooth four-dimensional case; the topological version is settled, this one is not.

summary: Is every problem whose solution can be checked quickly also solvable quickly? P versus NP and related complexity conjectures.
note: Famous Millennium problem; major breakthrough needed, no plausible clever argument.

summary: Do all nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function have real part one half?
note: Famous Millennium problem; decades of expert work, needs a major breakthrough.

summary: In a prime-factor-based construction sequence starting with 1, after the term 5 is there another prime term?
note: Can be settled by search if a prime term exists; no structural proof method apparent.

summary: Starting from a value other than 1, does the prime-index-and-reversal recurrence ever fall into a loop?
note: Dynamical question with no known invariant; search can only suggest, not prove, looping.

summary: Iterate n plus digit sum until a multiple of n appears: is the result never zero for any n?
note: Modular dynamics of a digit-sum map; a short invariant argument might settle it.

summary: For each n, is there a k such that k and n-1 linear forms like jk plus j minus 1 are all prime?
note: Dickson-type prime k-tuple statement; far beyond current prime sieve techniques.

summary: Starting from 1, each term is the previous term squared plus 2. When is the next prime term after the fifth?
note: Answer needs primality tests on enormous numbers; no proof, only computation.

summary: Do all odd numbers 2n+1 for n at least 4 split as 2p+q with odd primes p and q?
note: Goldbach-type ternary prime statement; circle-method results are asymptotic only.

summary: Is the smallest power with base above 1 and exponent n free of digit zero absent for n equal to 40?
note: Nonexistence over infinitely many bases; heuristic finiteness with no proof method.

summary: Do the ternary representations of powers of two contain at least one zero digit for all n above 15?
note: Digit patterns of powers of two are deep; no known way to rule out zero-free expansions.

summary: Between consecutive odd squares-related values, if n terms lie between 2n+1 and 2n+3, is one a product of two primes?
note: Goldbach-like semiprime gap claim; no known structural argument.

summary: Five starting values give recurrences that never merge. Is it true that infinitely many non-merging starting values exist?
note: Checked numerically to 10^8 only; proof of non-merging for all terms is out of reach.

summary: Sums of consecutive primes from index n to 2n form squares only for n equal to 3, 6, or 4072?
note: Finite list claim needs Diophantine control of prime sums; search alone cannot close it.

summary: Does the p-adic valuation of the imaginary part of a product of Gaussian-style factors grow like n over p minus 1 for primes p equal 1 mod 4?
note: Valuation asymptotics of a product; Legendre-style counting may apply, plausibly tractable.

summary: Sum of squares of nonacci numbers: which index gives the next prime term after the eighth term?
note: Asks for a specific value found by search; no proof structure.

summary: Is 509203 the smallest Riesel number, the first odd k where k times 2 to the m minus 1 is never prime?
note: Settled by covering-set and primality computations on huge numbers, not by a clever proof.

summary: Are there prime digit sums of Fermat numbers 2 to the 2 to the n plus 1 beyond n equal to 11?
note: Needs primality of huge Fermat-number digit sums; heuristic, decided by computation at best.

summary: Numbers n with phi(n) equal to phi(n plus phi(n)): is every term except the first even?
note: Parity of totient values might yield a clean argument; not yet seen.

summary: Is 1155 the last odd number in the sequence of n with perfect deficiency at most 10?
note: Needs control over all larger n; only finite search is available.

summary: For n above 3, is a certain numerator divisible by n squared exactly when n is prime?
note: Converse direction is Giuga-type and long open; the prime direction alone is classical.

summary: Binary strings marking prime positions: are a(2) and a(121) the only prime terms?
note: Finding more prime terms is a search; no method to prove there are no more.

summary: Does this recursive sequence on positive integers contain every positive integer?
note: Surjectivity of a recursive sequence; a greedy-style construction might work.

summary: Starting at 2, terms are the running lcm plus or minus 1. Are there infinitely many primes among the terms?
note: Euclid-style idea, but the lcm plus or minus 1 need not be prime; no guarantee.

summary: Greatest prime of form k(n-k)+1 for k up to n/2: is it zero only for n equal to 1, 6, 30, 54?
note: Needs prime values of a quadratic family for all n; Hardy-Littlewood-level input.

summary: Is the greatest prime of form k(n-k)-1 positive for every n above 3?
note: Existence of primes in a quadratic family; sieve methods fall short.

summary: Is the count of primes of form k(n-k)-1 positive for every n above 3?
note: Same claim as the previous entry, in count form; sieve methods fall short.

summary: Which positive integers cannot be written as a sum of two indices n with a(n) equal to 1? Conjectured exceptions are 1 through 7, 9, 11.
note: Goldbach-like if the index set is prime; the definition of a(n) needs checking.

summary: Does every odd number appear as lcm(1..n) divided by the denominator of the harmonic number H(n)?
note: Arithmetic of harmonic denominators; a targeted construction for odd m might work.

summary: Sierpinski's conjecture: the smallest m with no primes between nm and n(m+1) satisfies m at least n.
note: Prime-gap-type statement for all n; well beyond current prime distribution results.

summary: Do absolute values of this prime-difference combination cover every nonnegative even number and 1?
note: Needs control over prime gaps at all scales; no known method.

summary: Is the integer part of prime(n) divided by pi(n) decreasing infinitely often as n grows?
note: Needs small prime gaps at the right places; plausible with gap results, not settled.

summary: Colton's conjecture: refactorable numbers up to n outnumber half the primes up to n, for all n.
note: Zelinsky proved large n; a finite range up to about 7e13 remains, needing heavy computation.

summary: Digit count of n raised to its digit sum: besides 1 and 32, are there other fixed points?
note: A digit-count bound makes fixed points finite, so a short search settles it.

summary: For each n, the least m with 2 to the n minus m and 2 to the n plus m both prime: is m at most order n cubed?
note: Prime pairs symmetric about a power of two; Goldbach-type difficulty.

summary: Ascending-descending power transform of squares: after the prime term a(2)=5, what is the next prime term?
note: Answer is found by search on huge powers; no proof structure.

summary: Ascending-descending power transform of factorials: is there a nontrivial perfect power after a(4)=5^3?
note: Settled only by searching enormous values; no known structural handle.

summary: Ascending-descending power transform of 2^n: after prime terms at indices 1, 3, 4, what is the next prime-valued term?
note: Search-based; the OEIS comment conflicts with the formula, so the index must be checked.

summary: Are there prime powers q with q and q plus 2 both prime powers but neither prime, beyond one million?
note: Perfect-power pairs differing by two; Pillai-type Diophantine problem, no clear route.

summary: In the powers-of-two sequence, does the difference 1 occur infinitely often, meaning 2 to the n plus 1 is an odd semiprime infinitely often?
note: Semiprime values of 2 to the n plus 1; sieve results of Chen type fall short.

summary: Is the term a(33900) the last term equal to 1 in this largest-odd-divisor recurrence?
note: Specific-term search; a proof of no later 1s is not in reach.

summary: Is zeta(2n) divided by zeta(n) squared irrational for every odd n above 1?
note: Irrationality of zeta-values at odd arguments is open; no known technique.

summary: Are the only integers k with k to the fourth minus 1 dividing 2 to the k minus 1 the powers 2 to the 2 to the n?
note: Full classification of a divisibility family; no structural argument available.

summary: Are the partial sums of squared central binomial coefficients, as polynomials in x, irreducible over the rationals for every n?
note: Irreducibility of a family; a Newton-polygon or prime-reduction argument might work.

summary: Does the count of primes among k squared plus 3k plus 1 up to 10 to the n grow like 1.77 times the prime count?
note: Prime values of a quadratic with an exact asymptotic constant; far beyond current theory.

summary: Could the first n+1 digits of pi, read as an integer, ever form a perfect square? Haken conjectured no.
note: Heuristic probability argument; proof would need deep normality facts about pi.

summary: Do the fractional parts of sigma_k(n) divided by n to the k stay pairwise distinct for different n, for each k at least 2?
note: Infinite family of distinctness claims; no known way to control all n.

summary: Partial sums of 3 to the j plus minus 2 to the j: after known prime terms at 11, 17, 71, 91, 431, what is the next prime index?
note: Answer is a search over large values; no proof structure.

summary: Ratio of positive to negative determinants of consecutive prime blocks converges to a limit between 0.8 and 0.9?
note: Statistical limit tied to prime distribution; numeric evidence only.

summary: Is the number of primes in row n of the triangle k squared minus k plus p_n less than n for n above 13?
note: Modular covering of quadratic values; a residue-class argument may settle it.

summary: For every n at least 1, is there a k with the cyclotomic polynomial value at n prime?
note: Needs prime values of cyclotomic polynomials for every n; Bunyakovsky-type, open.

summary: Are there infinitely many primes of form 2 to the 2 to the n plus 2 to the n minus 1?
note: Fermat-type prime family; infinitude is an open problem in general.

summary: For each n at least 2, is there a k with 2 times n to the k minus 1 prime?
note: Exponential prime-value question for every n; Schinzel-type, no known method.

summary: In the half-Fibonacci sequence, do even terms have natural density one half, and do consecutive terms differ by one infinitely often?
note: Parity dynamics might give density; the consecutive-difference claim is less clear.

summary: Among the first n primes, is the count with odd binary weight at least the count with even binary weight, for n above 3?
note: Thue-Morse-type bias on primes; needs deep analytic prime results.

summary: For prime p with p minus 2 not prime, does the LCM recurrence give a(p-1) equal to p?
note: Structural LCM recurrence; an exact identity might be provable.

summary: Is the factorial distance to the nearest square bounded above by a constant for all n at least 2?
note: Needs n factorial to stay far from squares; Diophantine approximation, not elementary.

summary: In the Collatz step-difference sequence, is the liminf fraction of zero terms above one half?
note: Collatz-related density claim; no known method for Collatz statistics.

summary: Every large odd integer seems to be a prime 1 mod 6 plus a power of 2 plus eleven times a power of 2.
note: Goldbach-type additive problem with primes; needs circle-method-level analytic input.

summary: For each k at least 3, are there infinitely many primes of the form n^k + m^k + 1 with positive n and m?
note: Prime values of a two-variable polynomial of degree at least 3; no known method.
